text:
maria: Heads up — Legal asked for a CSV export of routing/quota policy changes that shows who changed what and when. Current export only gives diffs. They need a per-change, human-readable export (timestamp, actor, org, policy id, field, old/new). Can we do that without blowing up storage?

alex: We do persist immutable change events under events.change.* with a 'diff' object and sometimes a full snapshot reference. API today returns diff only. We could add ?include_full=true to the export endpoint to expand diffs into full rows, but size is the main concern. Thoughts on retention/size?

jamal: include_full=true will explode for policies with many routes. For big customers that's gigabytes. Options: 1) include_full only when snapshot exists and within retention window, 2) stream to cloud storage and return presigned link, 3) provide an expanded CSV where repeated fields are flattened into multiple rows. Also need to redact any secret fields (k8s creds, webhook tokens) before export.

maria: Legal specifically wants a CSV ingestable into their compliance tool (no JSON). Example columns they asked for: timestamp,user_email,org_id,policy_id,field_path,old_value,new_value,change_reason,trace_id. Having trace_id would let them correlate to request logs.

alex: Proposed pipeline: query change events by time range -> for each event expand diff to rows -> if include_full=true, fetch snapshot from snapshot-store for context -> stream rows to S3/GCS -> return presigned link. Console should have a checkbox "Include full snapshots (may be large)" and a size estimate. We'll need an async job + status endpoint.

janet: Can we ensure every change event stores request_trace_id and actor_ip? SRE needs that for investigations. If trace_id is missing, UX should show "trace not available" and the CSV should leave that column blank. Also add a column for policy_version/route_hash so we can reconcile.

infra-bot: change-export-service v1.2 deployed to canary on platform-prod :rocket:

maria: Also need a retention mapping column — customers must see whether an event is still retained in full or was truncated/redacted. e.g., retention_status = {"full","partial","redacted"}. Legal wants to know if older events were summarized.

jamal: CSV flattening notes: newline characters in JSON fields will break naive CSVs. I'll prototype a safe flattening that 1) JSON-escape complex values and 2) expand arrays into repeated rows. If we include snapshots, we should add a snapshot_link column instead of inlining huge blobs. I can mock a sample CSV generator by EOD and ping @alex for API knobs.

alex: Sounds good. Also plan to add columns: actor_ip, user_agent (if available), policy_version, route_hash, export_job_id. Default presigned link expiry = 7 days but make that configurable. We'll need doc updates: Audit -> Exports -> CSV schema and retention semantics.

maria: UX copy: warn that including full snapshots may contain personally identifiable data and increase export size. Provide a checkbox to redact personal data (email/phone) at export time.

jamal: Quick question — do we need per-field typed diffs in CSV? Legal prefers strings, but dev tools might want typed JSON. Maybe provide two formats: CSV for Legal and NDJSON for internal debugging.

alex: I like that. CSV = compliance; NDJSON = dev/export for engineers. We'll implement same expand/stream pipeline, just different serializer.

maria: OK. Action items: jamal to prototype CSV flattening (POC + sample), alex to spec API/console changes and export-job status, janet to confirm which telemetry fields we must include for incident linking, and I'll draft UX copy + legal checklist. Ping me in thread when POC is up. :+1:

janet: I'll check with SRE compliance checklist and post required telemetry fields by EOD.

alex: I'll open a short RFC with schema + API shape and link the POC when ready.

infra-bot: export-job-runner v0.9 scheduled for rollout tonight (non-blocking).

maria: Thanks all — leaving this thread open for RFC link and POC.
